record.original_question: For the update modification type U, which allows arbitrary modifications, determine the entire spectrum S(st,ss,pr,U): the set of triples (k,l,m) that can occur as stable, semi-stable, and preferred characteristics of the same argumentation framework and target set. In particular, decide whether the spectrum is exactly all monotonically decreasing triples with k>=l>=m.

evidence.quote: The second open problem regarding spectra and fibres is with respect to arbitrary modifications, so-called updates [8, Definition 5].

artifact.status_search_result: The problem concerns the spectrum S(st, ss, pr, U) for arbitrary update-type modifications in abstract argumentation. Foundational work on spectra (Baumann, "Spectra in Abstract Argumentation: An Analysis of Minimal Change") introduces the framework, and the question of characterizing the update spectrum is listed as an open problem with a conjecture that it is m.d.s.-complete. No subsequent publication confirming or refuting this conjecture was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Spectra in Abstract Argumentation: An Analysis of Minimal Change
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces spectra and characteristics for abstract argumentation semantics under different modification types; investigation of spectra reveals relationships among semantics.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational work defining spectra but not resolving the update-type spectrum S(st,ss,pr,U).

status_evidence.title: Characterizing change in abstract argumentation systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies change/dynamics in abstract argumentation; does not characterize the update spectrum for stable, semi-stable, and preferred semantics jointly.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on change does not resolve the conjecture.
